issues.title: Reversed inclusion for the holomorphic extension domain
issues.failure_explanation: Assumption ass:diffusion_matrix requires the real cube U to lie in the compact complex extension set K. The old theorem additionally requires K to lie in U. Hence K collapses to U, whose interior in C^d is empty, so it cannot provide the complex neighborhood used for the claimed extension or contain the downstream Bernstein polyellipses.
issues.overall_effect: The main theorem has no usable complex extension region as stated, and its three approximation corollaries cannot invoke it under their polyellipse hypotheses.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the clause “K is contained in U” in thm:mainthm by “U is contained in K.” No proof change is needed, and cor:maincor, cor:LS, and cor:CS may then invoke the theorem under their stated polyellipse hypotheses.
issues.why_classification: The opposite inclusion is uniquely forced by Assumption ass:diffusion_matrix, the proof's use of a complex neighborhood, and the dependent polyellipse hypotheses. The argument never uses the reversed inclusion, so this is a transcriptional reversal with no loss of guarantee.

issues.title: Original matrix used on the complex extension domain
issues.failure_explanation: The original matrix map is defined from C on the real parameter domain, while z ranges over the complex set H. Thus M(t,z) in eq:bound_term has no stated interface there. The proof instead constructs tilde M(t,z) from the holomorphic extension tilde C and derives the bound with that object. Consequently, the old displayed constant does not match the matrix map actually used by the proof.
issues.overall_effect: The holomorphy part of the theorem remains supported, but its stated uniform-bound constant and the B-dependent best-term and compressed-sensing corollaries use an undefined or mismatched matrix map.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: In eq:bound_term, replace M(t,z) by the already constructed holomorphic extension tilde M(t,z), defined from tilde C, W, and D, and use that corrected bound constant consistently in cor:maincor and cor:CS.
issues.why_classification: The old proof explicitly defines tilde M on the complex domain and derives the bound with it; the real-domain map M has no interface at z. Thus the proof uniquely forces a notation correction, with no repaired inference or weakened bound.

issues.title: Unbound exponent parameter in the least-squares results
issues.failure_explanation: The quantified data in th:main_ls do not include p, yet its conclusion contains C(rho,p) and the exponent 1/2-1/p. No range is inherited from another formal statement. Thus the assertion has no defined invocation range, unlike the old coefficient and compressed-sensing estimates, which explicitly quantify p.
issues.overall_effect: Neither the auxiliary least-squares theorem nor its diffusion corollary states the range over which its advertised algebraic rate is asserted.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Bind p in both th:main_ls and cor:LS by stating that the displayed estimate holds for every 0<p<1, leaving the sampling condition, probability, noise term, and algebraic exponent otherwise unchanged.
issues.why_classification: The unbound parameter makes the estimates formally unusable, and its precise range is not uniquely supplied by the old statements, so this is not merely transcriptional. Adding the standard range supported by the cited least-squares estimate is a short, routine local repair that preserves the intended method and rate.

issues.title: Missing amplitude factor in the least-squares bounds
issues.failure_explanation: Let the noise vanish and take a holomorphic polynomial having more nonzero orthonormal coefficients than the allowed cardinality of S. Its distance from every admissible polynomial space is positive. Multiplying it by an arbitrary scalar multiplies that distance, while the old right-hand side C(rho,p)(m/log(m/epsilon))^(1/2-1/p) is unchanged. Equation eq:bounderror shows the required dependence on the extension norm. For the diffusion specialization, linearity in the initial condition produces the same contradiction, and eq:bound_term provides the corresponding B scale.
issues.overall_effect: Both the general auxiliary estimate and its diffusion specialization understate errors for arbitrarily scaled functions or initial conditions, although their sampling regime and convergence exponent remain recoverable.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Multiply the approximation term in th:main_ls by the extension amplitude ||tilde f|| on the Bernstein polyellipse. In cor:LS, multiply the corresponding term by the established uniform extension bound B for the diffusion map. Retain the same sampling regime, probability, convergence exponent, and noise term.
issues.why_classification: The repair is local and follows directly from the coefficient estimate, but it withdraws the substantive amplitude-independent error guarantee asserted for arbitrary holomorphic functions and initial data. The resulting homogeneous bounds are recognizably the same least-squares results and preserve their rates, so the loss is limited and no global reconstruction is required.

issues.title: Unsupported uniform quantification in the auxiliary least-squares theorem

failure_location.quote: with probability at least $1 - \epsilon$ for any $f: \mathcal{U} \rightarrow \mathbb{C}$

diagnostic_evidence.quote: the support $S$ of the best $s$-term approximation to $f$

issues.failure_explanation: The old statement claims one set S and one probability statement for any holomorphically extendable f. The proof fixes f and chooses S from that function's best s-term approximation, establishing at most a function-dependent assertion with an event that may depend on f. Thus the proof supports a fixed-f guarantee, not the stated simultaneous guarantee.
issues.overall_effect: The auxiliary theorem does not establish a uniform least-squares guarantee over the whole function class. Its application to the single fixed diffusion map in cor:LS does not require that stronger uniformity.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Reorder the theorem's quantifiers: for each fixed holomorphically extendable f, choose the approximation set S=S(f) and assert probability at least 1−epsilon for the sampling event associated with that fixed f. Do not claim that one S and one event work simultaneously for the entire function class.
issues.why_classification: This locally matches the proof and leaves the fixed-function rate, sampling budget, and noise guarantee intact, but it relinquishes the substantially stronger simultaneous uniform guarantee over all f. The surviving fixed-f theorem is recognizably comparable and requires no new proof architecture, making the issue moderate rather than minor or serious.
